column3: God is revealed through Nakayama Miki, who is chosen as the Shrine of God (1838); in 1854 she begins to administer the Grant for Safe Childbirth and recruit her first followers.
Nakayama dies in 1887; Izo Iburi's oral revelations, collected as the Osashizu, continue to 1907.
Tenrikyo is recognised as one of the thirteen groups of Sect Shinto (1908), and becomes the first new religion in Japan to do social work.
The designation as a group of Sect Shinto ends (1945); followers in Japan reach a high of 2,298,420 in 1974.
Tenrikyo is estimated at over 2 million followers worldwide (2002); in Japan 1,121,541 are counted in 2025.
